title: Azure Local, Discovery to Day 2
subtitle: Hybrid Cloud: Plan, Deploy, and Operate Azure Local from Discovery to Day 2
followAlongPolicy: Mostly watch and read. Full follow-along only where no cluster is needed: the Surveyor assessment on the synthetic workbook, the Trailwright design record and its infrastructure.yml export, and the Bicep what-if. Every other demo is a read-along with the repo path.

variables.name: <sub>
variables.meaning: your Azure Local landing-zone subscription id

sections.title: Open — the voyage and the ship

demos.title: Workload assessment in Surveyor (RVTools route)

followAlong.goal: Import a synthetic RVTools workbook into Azure Local Surveyor and read the inventory totals.
needs: The synthetic workbook IIC-RVTools-demo.xlsx from the repo (src/assessment)

steps.title: Open Surveyor and enter the target hardware
steps.instructions: Open Azure Local Surveyor, go to Workload Planning > Assess existing hardware, and enter the target nodes (CPU, RAM, drives). Do not enter the source VMware hosts.
steps.check: The target hardware is saved in the project.

steps.title: Import the workbook
steps.instructions: Go to Workloads > Import RVTools and select the workbook. An import replaces existing inventory rows, so save any existing project first.
steps.check: The preview reports 24 VMs, 3 skipped templates or placeholders and 2 powered-off VMs included.

steps.title: Use the inventory and read the totals
steps.instructions: Confirm Use this inventory. The dashboard shows allocated demand.
steps.check: 72 vCPU, 160 GiB memory, 3 TiB consumed and 5.8 TiB provisioned storage.

steps.title: Review the two legacy VMs
steps.instructions: Open the two iic-legacy VMs. Decide whether to keep them in the estate and note that they have no performance history.
steps.check: You can state which evidence is missing for each.

troubleshooting: Counts differ: check the workbook version and that you imported the vInfo tab from the supplied file.
TiB and decimal TB are different units; compare like with like.
cleanup: Save the project or discard it.

demos.title: Azure Migrate discovery (animation)

followAlong.goal: Understand the Azure Migrate discovery route to Azure Local.

steps.title: Read the overview and prerequisites
steps.instructions: Read the Azure Migrate overview for VMware to Azure Local (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/migrate/migration-azure-migrate-vmware-overview) and the prerequisites (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/migrate/migrate-vmware-prerequisites): the Azure Migrate project is created in the Azure portal, and the Azure Local instance needs a logical network and a storage path.
steps.check: You can list the source-side and target-side prerequisites.

steps.title: Read the discovery steps
steps.instructions: Read Step 1 of 'Discover and replicate VMware VMs' (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/migrate/migrate-vmware-replicate): project key, source appliance, VDDK 8.0.x, vCenter credentials, onboarding to Azure Local, Start discovery.
steps.check: You know why agentless dependency analysis is switched off on this route.

demos.title: Sizing and fit against two nodes

followAlong.goal: Read the sizing result for the synthetic estate.
needs: The Surveyor project from the previous demo

steps.title: Open the fit and storage design
steps.instructions: Go to Fit & Recommendations, then Storage Design. Change the growth and the storage basis (provisioned or consumed) and observe the result.
steps.check: Planned storage changes with the basis you choose; note decimal TB versus TiB.

demos.title: Whole-site fabric evidence and Network ATC intent design

followAlong.goal: Trace reviewed whole-site evidence into the approved intent design without overwriting decisions.

demos.title: Trailwright: the design record becomes infrastructure.yml

followAlong.goal: Open the IIC design record in Trailwright, let validation catch a bad value, fix it and export the infrastructure file.
needs: No cluster and no Azure subscription required
The IIC Trailwright project from the repo (src/design/trailwright-iic-example.trailwright.json), the same file the presenter opens; or your own design values

steps.title: Open Trailwright and the IIC project
steps.instructions: Open Azure Local Trailwright (labs.hybridsolutions.cloud/azurelocal-trailwright) and open the IIC project file from the repo (src/design/trailwright-iic-example.trailwright.json). To use your own design instead, start a new project with a connected, hyperconverged deployment of two machines.
steps.check: The project summary shows the IIC answers: nodes, storage, intents, identity, connectivity and landing zone.

steps.title: Shorten the management pool to five addresses
steps.instructions: In the management network step, change the end address so the IP pool holds only five addresses.
steps.check: Validation reports that the pool needs at least six contiguous addresses and links the Microsoft Learn source.

steps.title: Fix the pool and check the design
steps.instructions: Widen the pool to six or more addresses (or restore the original end address), then review the network intents, identity and connectivity steps.
steps.check: The validation summary has no errors.

steps.title: Export the infrastructure file
steps.instructions: Export infrastructure.yml (and, if you want, the Bicep parameter starting point) and open it in an editor.
steps.check: Each design answer appears as a value in the file.

troubleshooting: A step is missing: it appears only when an earlier answer needs it; check the deployment type and storage connectivity answers.
The export is a starting point: review every value before you use it with a deployment template.
cleanup: Save the project file locally or discard it; nothing is stored in Azure.

demos.title: Cloud-driven deployment: the what-if

followAlong.goal: Generate and preview an Azure Local deployment without creating anything.
needs: PowerShell 7 with the Az.Accounts and Az.KeyVault modules
Copies of the two example environment files with your values

steps.title: Prepare the config
steps.instructions: Copy the two example environment files (shared values and Azure Local values) and replace the values with yours: names, nodes, IP pool, VLANs.
steps.command:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force environment/shared, environment/azure-local | Out-Null
Copy-Item automation/shared/examples/environment.shared.example.yml environment/shared/environment.yml
Copy-Item automation/shared/examples/environment.azure-local.example.yml environment/azure-local/environment.yml
steps.check: Both files exist under environment/. Edit them before you go on.

steps.title: Check the config
steps.instructions: Load the automation module and read the Azure Local scope back.
steps.check: The command returns without errors.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.instructions: The what-if runs against your subscription and creates nothing. The script reads through Az PowerShell and runs the what-if with the Azure CLI, so sign in to both.
steps.command:
Connect-AzAccount -Subscription <sub>
az login
az account set --subscription <sub>
steps.check: Get-AzContext and az account show both name your subscription.

steps.title: Run the validate pass as a dry run
steps.instructions: Run the Validate pass without -Execute. It generates the parameter files, builds the templates and runs a what-if.
steps.check: The template build passes and a what-if result is printed; no resources were created.

steps.title: Read what the what-if cannot see
steps.instructions: Compare the output with the Environment Checker results. Platform-side checks run only during the Validate pass in Azure.
steps.check: You can list one check the what-if does not cover.

troubleshooting: Missing providers: register the resource providers listed in the landing-zone README first.
Input file not found: run the script without -Stage, so the Generate stage writes the parameter files first.
az exited with code 1 or No Az context: sign in with az login and Connect-AzAccount.

demos.title: Azure Migrate: VMware to Azure Local (animation)

followAlong.goal: Read the migration procedure end to end.

steps.title: Replicate
steps.instructions: Read Steps 2 and 3 of 'Discover and replicate VMware VMs' (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/migrate/migrate-vmware-replicate): target appliance, replicate (up to 10 VMs per batch; logical network, storage path, VHDX), seed disks, Ready to migrate.
steps.check: You know what the storage account holds (metadata only) and where the disk data goes.

steps.title: Migrate, verify, complete
steps.instructions: Read 'Migrate VMware VMs to Azure Local' (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/migrate/migrate-vmware-migrate): migrate with the source shut down, verify in the portal and the guest, Complete migration, clean up, enable guest management.
steps.check: You can say why Complete migration matters (seed disks and replication state).

steps.title: Check the limits
steps.instructions: Read the migration FAQ (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/migrate/migrate-faq): batches, boot type, static IPs, Arc agent reuse. Hyper-V sources follow the same pattern as a preview (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/migrate/migration-azure-migrate-overview).
steps.check: You know which source VMs need preparation (BitLocker, shared disks, Linux integration services).

demos.title: Signal to diagnosis: the Observability Agent investigates the drive fault (preview)

followAlong.goal: Investigate an Azure Monitor alert with the Azure Copilot Observability Agent (preview) in your own subscription.
needs: Access to Azure Copilot in your tenant
An Azure Monitor workspace associated with the subscription (it holds the issues)
Issue Contributor, Monitoring Contributor or Contributor on that workspace to save an issue
A fired Azure Monitor alert in a region where the agent is available

steps.title: Start an investigation from an alert
steps.instructions: Open a fired alert in Azure Monitor > Alerts and select Investigate. Confirm the scope the agent proposes.
steps.check: The agent reports its plan, then findings, hypotheses ruled out and next steps.

steps.title: Keep the result
steps.instructions: Select Create issue to save the investigation as an Azure Monitor issue in your Azure Monitor workspace.
steps.check: The issue is listed under Monitor > Issues with the investigation attached.

troubleshooting: Asked for an Azure Monitor workspace: associate the subscription with one (once per subscription).
No Investigate action: check that your account has Azure Copilot access.
cleanup: Close or delete test issues; chat and investigations are billed per use.

demos.title: Fault 3: node failure (animation)

followAlong.goal: Read what a node failure does on a two-node instance and how to prove recovery.

steps.title: Quorum
steps.instructions: Read 'Understanding cluster and pool quorum' (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/storage/storage-spaces/quorum): two nodes with a witness survive one node failure, not a second.
steps.check: You can say why a two-node instance needs a witness.

steps.title: VMs and GPUs
steps.instructions: Read 'Virtual machine resiliency for Azure Local' (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/manage/disaster-recovery-vm-resiliency) and the DDA note in 'Use GPUs with clustered VMs' (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/deploy/use-gpu-with-clustered-vm).
steps.check: You know why a node failure restarts VMs instead of live-migrating them, and where a DDA VM can restart.

steps.title: Storage resync and the checks
steps.instructions: Read 'Understand and monitor storage resync' (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/storage/storage-spaces/understand-storage-resync) and the resume and resync steps of 'Failover cluster maintenance procedures' (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/manage/maintain-servers).
steps.check: You can name the commands that prove recovery: Get-StorageJob empty, Get-VirtualDisk Healthy.
